## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r, plotting 2022 and 2026 rain data}

library(ggplot2)

precip_2022$event <- "Dec 2022 / Jan 2023"
precip_2026$event <- "Jan 2026"

combined_precip <- bind_rows(precip_2022, precip_2026) %>%
  group_by(event) %>%
  mutate(day_num = row_number()) %>%  # aligns both events on a comparable x-axis
  ungroup()

monthly_precip_2022_2026 =ggplot(combined_precip, aes(x = day_num, y = value, fill = event)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    title = "Daily Precipitation: Dec 2022/Jan 2023 vs Jan 2026",
    x = "Day of Event Window",
    y = "Precipitation (inches)",
    fill = "Event"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```

```{r}
# Reusable NOAA GHCND daily precip puller
# (was called as get_noaa_precip() but never defined in the .Rmd —
#  adding it here so the file is self-contained and knits cleanly)
# ============================================================
get_noaa_precip <- function(start_date, end_date, station_id, token) {
  api_endpoint <- "https://www.ncdc.noaa.gov/cdo-web/api/v2/data"
 
  # NOAA CDO API caps each request at 1 year AND 1000 records, so for
  # long windows we chunk by month and stack — safer than one big call
  month_starts <- seq(as.Date(start_date), as.Date(end_date), by = "month")
 
  purrr::map_dfr(month_starts, function(m_start) {
    m_end <- min(lubridate::ceiling_date(m_start, "month") - 1, as.Date(end_date))
 
    resp <- httr::GET(api_endpoint,
      httr::add_headers(token = token),
      query = list(
        datasetid  = "GHCND",
        stationid  = station_id,
        startdate  = format(m_start, "%Y-%m-%d"),
        enddate    = format(m_end, "%Y-%m-%d"),
        datatypeid = "PRCP",
        units      = "standard",
        limit      = 1000
      ))
 
    if (httr::status_code(resp) != 200) {
      warning(paste("NOAA API returned", httr::status_code(resp), "for", m_start))
      return(tibble::tibble())
    }
 
    parsed <- jsonlite::fromJSON(httr::content(resp, "text", encoding = "UTF-8"))
    if (is.null(parsed$results)) return(tibble::tibble())
 
    parsed$results %>%
      dplyr::mutate(date = as.Date(date), value = as.numeric(value)) %>%
      dplyr::select(date, value)
  })
}
```



```{r, 2022 NOAA monthly summary pull}

# ============================================================
# Pull both years
# ============================================================
library(lubridate)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
 
today <- Sys.Date()
end_date_2026 <- min(as.Date("2026-06-30"), today)
 
precip_full2022 <- get_noaa_precip("2022-07-01", "2023-06-30", "GHCND:USW00023272", cdo_token)
precip_full2026 <- get_noaa_precip("2025-07-01", as.character(end_date_2026), "GHCND:USW00023272", cdo_token)
 
# sanity check before plotting — confirm you actually have ~12 months each
precip_full2022 %>% mutate(month = floor_date(date, "month")) %>% count(month) %>% print(n = 20)
precip_full2026 %>% mutate(month = floor_date(date, "month")) %>% count(month) %>% print(n = 20)
 
# ============================================================
# Aggregate to monthly totals — CONSISTENT NAMING, both years
# ============================================================
monthly_data2022 <- precip_full2022 %>%
  mutate(month = floor_date(date, "month")) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(monthly_total_in = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(complete = "Complete")  # full window already closed, nothing partial
 
monthly_data2026 <- precip_full2026 %>%
  mutate(month = floor_date(date, "month")) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(monthly_total_in = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(complete = ifelse(month == floor_date(today, "month"), "Partial month", "Complete"))
 
# ============================================================
# Shared axis limits so both plots are directly comparable
# ============================================================
shared_y_limits <- c(0, max(monthly_data2022$monthly_total_in,
                             monthly_data2026$monthly_total_in, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05)
 
plot_2022 <- ggplot(monthly_data2022, aes(x = month, y = monthly_total_in, fill = complete)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Complete" = "steelblue", "Partial month" = "gray70"), drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b %Y", date_breaks = "1 month",
               limits = as.Date(c("2022-07-01", "2023-06-30"))) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = shared_y_limits) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Precipitation: July 2022 – June 2023",
    subtitle = stringr::str_wrap("Source: NOAA NCEI, San Francisco Downtown Station GHCND:USW00023272 | https://www.weather.gov/wrh/climate?wfo=mtr", width = 60),
    x = "Month", y = "Total Precipitation (inches)", fill = "complete"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "gray40"))

ggsave("monthly_precip_2022_2023.png", plot = plot_2022, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# Overlaid comparison plot — aligned by month-of-water-year (Jul=1...Jun=12)
# so the two years sit side by side regardless of calendar year
# ============================================================
water_year_month <- function(d) {
  m <- month(d)
  # July -> 1, ... Dec -> 6, Jan -> 7, ... Jun -> 12
  ((m - 7) %% 12) + 1
}
 
combined_monthly <- bind_rows(
  monthly_data2022 %>% mutate(water_year = "2022–2023"),
  monthly_data2026 %>% mutate(water_year = "2025–2026")
) %>%
  mutate(
    wy_month_num = water_year_month(month),
    wy_month_label = factor(month.abb[((wy_month_num - 1 + 6) %% 12) + 1],
                             levels = month.abb[c(7:12, 1:6)])  # Jul...Jun order
  )
 
overlay_plot <- ggplot(combined_monthly, aes(x = wy_month_label, y = monthly_total_in,
                                              fill = water_year, alpha = complete)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c("Complete" = 1, "Partial month" = 0.5), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = shared_y_limits) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Precipitation, Overlaid by Water Year",
    subtitle = "Water year = Jul–Jun | Source: NOAA NCEI, San Francisco Downtown Station GHCND:USW00023272",
    x = "Month of Water Year", y = "Total Precipitation (inches)", fill = "Water Year"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
 
overlay_plot
 
ggsave("monthly_precip_overlay_2022_vs_2026.png", plot = overlay_plot,
       width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

```{r, let's try something (revisit this)}
# You need a date range or representative date for each Study.Phase
# Example structure - adjust to your actual phase-to-date mapping

phase_dates <- c_data %>%
    group_by(Study.Phase) %>%
  summarise(
    start_date = min(Date.removed.from.field, na.rm = TRUE),
    end_date   = max(Date.removed.from.field, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Sum precipitation within each phase's date window
precip_by_phase <- phase_dates %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    total_precip = sum(
      precip_full2022$value[precip_full2022$date >= start_date &
                             precip_full2022$date <= end_date],
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Join precip onto your flux summary
time_dist_summary <- time_dist_summary %>%
   left_join(precip_by_phase %>% select(Study.Phase, total_precip), by = "Study.Phase")



ggplot(time_dist_summary, aes(x = Study.Phase)) +
  geom_col(aes(y = total_precip), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(aes(y = mean_flux, group = 1), method = "loess", se = FALSE, color = "darkred", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(y = mean_flux), color = "darkred", size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ Dist, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Precipitation (in)",
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ ., name = expression(Mean~Flux~(g/m^3)))
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  ) +
  labs(title = paste("Flux & Precipitation Through Time by Distance at", "Corte Madera"), x = "Study Phase")
)
```

```{r, tides 2022}
library(purrr)

get_noaa_water_level <- function(start_date, end_date, station = "9414290") {
  api_endpoint <- "https://api.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/api/prod/datagetter"
  resp <- GET(api_endpoint, query = list(
    begin_date = start_date,
    end_date = end_date,
    station = station,
    product = "water_level",
    datum = "MLLW",
    units = "english",
    time_zone = "lst_ldt",
    format = "json"
  ))
  fromJSON(content(resp, "text", encoding = "UTF-8"))$data %>%
    mutate(
      t = as.POSIXct(t, format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M", tz = "America/Los_Angeles"),
      v = as.numeric(v)
    ) %>%
    rename(datetime = t, water_level_ft = v) %>%
    select(datetime, water_level_ft)
}

# Build monthly date chunks for July 2022 - June 2023
month_starts <- seq(as.Date("2022-07-01"), as.Date("2023-06-01"), by = "month")
month_ends <- ceiling_date(month_starts, "month") - 1

# Pull each month and stack them
tide_full2022 <- map2_dfr(month_starts, month_ends, function(start, end) {
  get_noaa_water_level(format(start, "%Y%m%d"), format(end, "%Y%m%d"))
})
```
```{r}

monthly_tide2022 <- tide_full2022 %>%
  mutate(month = floor_date(as.Date(datetime), "month")) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(
    monthly_max_ft = max(water_level_ft, na.rm = TRUE),
    monthly_mean_ft = mean(water_level_ft, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}

ggplot(monthly_tide2022, aes(x = month, y = monthly_max_ft)) +
  geom_col(fill = "darkcyan") +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b %Y", date_breaks = "1 month") +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Maximum Water Level: July 2022 – June 2023", 
    subtitle = stringr::str_wrap("Source: NOAA CO-OPS, San Francisco Station 9414290 | https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/stationhome.html?id=9414290", width = 60),
    x = "Month", y = "Max Water Level (ft, MLLW)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```


```{r, tides 2026}

library(purrr)

get_noaa_water_level <- function(start_date, end_date, station = "9414290") {
  api_endpoint <- "https://api.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/api/prod/datagetter"
  resp <- GET(api_endpoint, query = list(
    begin_date = start_date,
    end_date = end_date,
    station = station,
    product = "water_level",
    datum = "MLLW",
    units = "english",
    time_zone = "lst_ldt",
    format = "json"
  ))
  fromJSON(content(resp, "text", encoding = "UTF-8"))$data %>%
    mutate(
      t = as.POSIXct(t, format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M", tz = "America/Los_Angeles"),
      v = as.numeric(v)
    ) %>%
    rename(datetime = t, water_level_ft = v) %>%
    select(datetime, water_level_ft)
}

# Build monthly date chunks for July 2025 - June 2026
month_starts <- seq(as.Date("2025-07-01"), as.Date("2026-06-01"), by = "month")
month_ends <- ceiling_date(month_starts, "month") - 1

# Pull each month and stack them
tide_full2025_6 <- map2_dfr(month_starts, month_ends, function(start, end) {
  get_noaa_water_level(format(start, "%Y%m%d"), format(end, "%Y%m%d"))
})

# monthly tide rates 2026
monthly_tide2026 <- tide_full2025_6 %>%
  mutate(month = floor_date(as.Date(datetime), "month")) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(
    monthly_max_ft = max(water_level_ft, na.rm = TRUE),
    monthly_mean_ft = mean(water_level_ft, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


tide_sf_2026 = ggplot(monthly_tide2026, aes(x = month, y = monthly_max_ft)) +
  geom_col(fill = "darkcyan") +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b %Y", date_breaks = "1 month") +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Maximum Water Level: July 2025 – June 2026",
    subtitle = stringr::str_wrap("Source: NOAA CO-OPS, San Francisco Station 9414290 | https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/stationhome.html?id=9414290", width = 60),
    x = "Month", y = "Max Water Level (ft, MLLW)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))


ggsave("tide_sf_2026.png", plot = tide_sf_2026, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```
